cases.rationale: proto2 explicit default changed: a reader of absent data sees a different value.
a field moved into a oneof changes its last-one-wins grouping.
the package qualifies every type name on the wire for Any and rpc paths.
adding a proto2 required field makes old messages fail to parse.
dropping a reserved enum number reopens it for reuse.
dropping a reserved field number reopens it for reuse.
a unary request becoming a stream changes the call protocol.
a unary response becoming a stream changes the call protocol.
the request message type changed.
the response message type changed.
the declared idempotency level is part of the rpc contract.
deleting an enum value without reserving its number allows unsafe reuse.
deleting a field without reserving its number allows unsafe reuse.
int32 (varint) and string (length-delimited) use different wire types.
sint32 zigzag encoding is not interchangeable with int32 varints.
field names never appear on the wire.
a new field number is ignored by old readers.
deleting a field whose number is reserved is the safe deletion.
a new enum number is additive.
deleting an enum value whose number is reserved is the safe deletion.
int32, int64, uint32, uint64 and bool share the varint wire type.
string and bytes share the length-delimited wire type.
fixed32 and sfixed32 share the 32-bit wire type.
json_name affects JSON only; WIRE does not check it.
a new rpc is additive.
comments never reach the wire.

derivation: Expected verdicts come from each pinned WIRE rule purpose (buf config ls-breaking-rules) and protobuf wire-format semantics, authored without running Buf and without reading Buf test data.

not_asserted.FIELD_WIRE_COMPATIBLE_CARDINALITY: Its stated purpose does not fix which singular/repeated/map transitions it reports; no golden asserts it until an independent truth is recorded.

unsupported_inputs: Path, encoding, size and count refusals are fenced by TestCheckerRejectsUnsafeOrUnboundedInputsBeforeExec; a source that fails to compile is a request error, never a verdict.
